logo_override.validation_detail: HTTP 200, content-type image/jpeg, 32106 bytes; rendered on a white background it shows the Flemish lion mark plus 'Vlaanderen / verbeelding werkt' in dark grey - a JPEG has no alpha channel so there is no white-on-transparent risk, and the wordmark is clearly legible on a light card

notes: The Flanders Trainee Programme is a programme of the Government of Flanders (Departement Buitenlandse Zaken), so the Government of Flanders mark is the correct awarding-body logo under rule 2 - a university mark would have been a provenance error. Found in the page's own JSON-LD, which declares publisher 'Vlaamse overheid' with logo ImageObject https://www.vlaanderen.be/img/logo/vlaanderen-logo.jpg - exactly the step-1 lookup the brief prescribes. Probed: 200 image/jpeg 32106 B, rendered and visually confirmed (lion + Vlaanderen/verbeelding werkt in dark grey). Rejected: the og:image and twitter:image https://assets.vlaanderen.be/image/upload/c_fill,h_630,q_auto:eco,w_1200/TWIT_card_algemeen_aw4mra, because assets.vlaanderen.be is a Cloudinary image CDN mirroring the file (rules 1 and 6) and it is a programme banner, not a logo; and the app icons on ui.vlaanderen.be/3.latest/icons/app-icon/icon-highres-precomposed.png (200, image/png, 8648 B - probed and rendered, shows only the black lion on the yellow Flemish flag tile, no wordmark). Note for the merge: www.vlaanderen.be is a live Nuxt app whose header logo is rendered client-side, so a plain HTML fetch of the page shows no logo at all - the JSON-LD is the reliable source here. Playwright's page.goto to this host timed out at 30s once, so webfetch was used to read the markup instead.
